title: CoupledStronglyConcaveMinimax.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The objective and coupled constraints may be nonconvex in x. No convexity assumption is imposed in the minimization variable.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CoupledStronglyConcaveMinimax.lean: Assumptions imposes strongly_concave and convex_constraints only in y.

problem_class.label: saddle_point
problem_class.details: Coupled constrained nonconvex–strongly-concave minimax formulation: minimize over x∈X and maximize f(x,y) over y∈Y subject to c(x,y)≤0. For every fixed x, f(x,·) is μ-strongly concave and each c_i(x,·) is convex; μ>0.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: A query z∈X×Y returns the exact full joint gradient ∇f(z). Replies are exact for every history and oracle seed at domain queries.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: The same query returns the exact objective value f(z).

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Each bundled oracle call also returns the full constraint vector c(z) and its exact Jacobian Dc(z). All Params fields—including domains, starting points, dimensions, bounds, μ, δ, Z, and ε—are public; the instance functions are hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CoupledStronglyConcaveMinimax.lean: Reply.constraints, Reply.jacobian, Assumptions.derivative, exactReply, spec.Public, and spec.publicInput.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: X⊆ℝ^nx and Y⊆ℝ^ny are nonempty compact convex sets with Euclidean geometry and diameter bounds DX and DY. Constraint vectors use the Euclidean norm in ℝ^constraints.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CoupledStronglyConcaveMinimax.lean: XSpace, YSpace, Weights, Joint, and Valid.compactX, compactY, convexX, convexY, startX, startY, diameterX, diameterY.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform qualification at every z∈X×Y: there exists a y-direction d with ‖d‖≤Z, ⟨n,d⟩≤0 for every n∈N_Y(y), and Dc_i(z)[0,d]≤−δ for every strictly violated constraint c_i(z)>0; Z,δ>0. Also ∇f is Lf-Lipschitz, Dc is LJ-Lipschitz, ‖Dc‖≤J, ‖∇_x f‖≤Gx, ‖∇_y f‖≤Gy, and ‖c‖≤C throughout the domain. These bounds are nonnegative.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CoupledStronglyConcaveMinimax.lean: Assumptions.qualification, gradient_lipschitz, jacobian_lipschitz, jacobian_bound, gradientX_bound, gradientY_bound, constraint_bound; Valid.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The returned point must satisfy ‖[c(x,y)]_+‖₂≤ε, together with exact membership in X×Y and nonnegative multipliers.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: All KKT requirements hold jointly almost surely under the output law. Convergence uses the product of the algorithm and oracle seed laws with a fixed oracle budget.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: Output (x,y,λ) must have x∈X, y∈Y, λ≥0, and ∑_i|λ_i c_i(x,y)|≤ε. Writing g=∇f−Dc*λ, there must exist n_x∈N_X(x), n_y∈N_Y(y) with ‖g_x+n_x‖≤ε and ‖g_y−n_y‖≤ε. These are unsquared normal-cone stationarity residuals at the returned point; ε>0.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The formulation combines nonlinear constraints coupling the minimization and maximization variables with a uniform qualification on strictly violated constraints and an output requiring stationarity, feasibility, and absolute componentwise complementarity.

descriptionHtml:
Coupled Strongly Concave Minimax

We consider minimizing over x∈X⊂Rnx the maximum of f(x,y) over y∈Y⊂Rny subject to c(x,y)≤0, where c has m components and nx,ny,m are nonnegative integers. The sets are compact and convex; f is strongly concave in y, potentially nonconvex in x, and each constraint is convex in y. Gradients and constraint Jacobians satisfy Lipschitz and boundedness conditions, together with a uniform constraint qualification. On X×Y, the oracle returns f, ∇f, c, and its Jacobian. For ε>0, the goal is an output in X×Y with nonnegative multipliers whose Euclidean constraint violation, absolute complementarity sum, and two normal-cone stationarity residuals are each at most ε, almost surely.

The optimization problem is minx∈X maxy∈Yc(x,y)≤0f(x,y). Write E=Rnx×Rny, D=X×Y, and let f:E→R and c:E→Rm. All vector norms are Euclidean, with the product norm ∥(x,y)∥=(∥x∥2+∥y∥2)1/2. Operator norms ∥⋅∥op are induced by these norms. The parameters satisfy Lf,LJ,J,Gx,Gy,C,DX,DY≥0,μ,δ,Z,ε>0. The algorithm receives the dimensions, sets X,Y, given points x0,y0, and all the displayed scalar parameters.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Domain and starting points). The sets X and Y are compact and convex, with x0∈X and y0∈Y. Their diameters satisfy ∥x−x′∥≤DX(x,x′∈X),∥y−y′∥≤DY(y,y′∈Y).

Assumption 2 (Differentiability and uniform bounds). The functions f and c are Fréchet differentiable at every point of D. Write A(z):E→Rm for the Jacobian of c at z. For all z,w∈D, ∥∇f(z)−∇f(w)∥≤Lf∥z−w∥,∥A(z)−A(w)∥op≤LJ∥z−w∥. For every z∈D, ∥A(z)∥op≤J,∥c(z)∥≤C,∥∇xf(z)∥≤Gx,∥∇yf(z)∥≤Gy.

Assumption 3 (Strong concavity and constraint convexity). For every x∈X and i∈{1,…,m}, the function y↦ci(x,y) is convex on Y. For every x∈X and y,y′∈Y, f(x,y′)≤f(x,y)+⟨∇yf(x,y),y′−y⟩−μ2∥y′−y∥2.

For a convex set S and u∈S, define its normal cone by NS(u)={n:⟨n,v−u⟩≤0 for every v∈S}.

Assumption 4 (Uniform constraint qualification). For every (x,y)∈D, there exists d∈Rny such that ∥d∥≤Z,⟨n,d⟩≤0for every n∈NY(y),[A(x,y)(0,d)]i≤−δwhenever ci(x,y)>0.

At a query z∈D, the oracle returns the exact tuple (f(z),∇f(z),c(z),A(z)). Queries take values in E; replies outside D are unspecified.

The output is a triple (x¯,y¯,λ¯)∈Rnx×Rny×Rm. Set z¯=(x¯,y¯) and r=∇f(z¯)−A(z¯)∗λ¯=(rx,ry), where A(z¯)∗ denotes the Euclidean adjoint. Define [c(z¯)]+ componentwise by [c(z¯)]+,i=max{ci(z¯),0}. The required accuracy is x¯∈X,y¯∈Y,λ¯≥0,∥[c(z¯)]+∥≤ε,∑i=1m|λ¯ici(z¯)|≤ε,∃nx∈NX(x¯), ny∈NY(y¯):∥rx+nx∥≤ε,∥ry−ny∥≤ε,P-a.s. Here P is the law of the algorithm and oracle randomness, taken independently, and the almost-sure requirement applies to all the displayed output conditions jointly.

comparisonHtml:
Consider minx∈Xmaxy∈Y,c(x,y)≤0f(x,y) on nonempty compact convex Euclidean sets, with supplied starts in X×Y. The gradient of f is Lf-Lipschitz, f(x,⋅) is μ-strongly concave, and each ci(x,⋅) is convex. The constraint Jacobian is LJ-Lipschitz; ∥Jc∥≤J, ∥∇xf∥≤Gx, ∥∇yf∥≤Gy, ∥c∥≤C; diameters are bounded by DX,DY. At every (x,y), some d∈NY(y)∘ satisfies ∥d∥≤Z and ⟨∇yci,d⟩≤−δ for every violated constraint. Here μ,δ,Z,ε>0. Target: deterministic ε-KKT, with λ≥0, ∥[c]+∥≤ε, ∑i|λici|≤ε, and normal-cone stationarity residuals at most ε for x and y. One complete oracle call returns (f,∇f,c,Jc).

Sufficient oracle budgets for CoupledStronglyConcaveMinimax.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) CoupledMinimaxCappedKkt (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O([1+B/μlog(2+BDYS(1+ε)ε)]×[1+B2ΔS2(1+ε)2με2])
(2) ALDER (Zhang et al. 2026, Theorem 16) O(1+ℓε3/2Hμε2) complete calls; 0<ε≤1, given a feasible start. Its construction cost is excluded. (1): ε−2log⁡(1/ε) instead of ε−7/2 for fixed remaining data and small ε; roughly ε≪μ2/3, up to logarithms. Fixed-cap stationarity transfers to KKT. (1): leading μ−3/2 instead of μ−1/2; can lose at moderate accuracy with small μ. Nested inner solves replace a single loop.
(3) FAL (Lu and Mei 2026, Theorem 2, Remark 6(ii)); specialization: no outer constraints, indicator composite terms, uniform inner Slater O(ε−7/2[1+log⁡(1/ε)]) gradient/Jacobian and projection operations, with remaining problem data fixed and sufficiently small ε; aggregate complementarity |λ⊤c|≤ε after rescaling the tolerance. (1): Scope: violated-only qualification replaces uniform inner Slater; permits paired equality constraints. The aggregate complementarity target in (3) prevents an identical-criterion rate comparison. (1) does not cover the outer nonlinear constraints or general proximal composite terms handled by (3).

Abbr: m is the number of coupled constraints; [c]+ is the componentwise positive part; NX,NY are outward normal cones and ∘ denotes the polar cone. Stationarity uses L=f−λ⊤c: ∥∇xL+nx∥,∥∇yL−ny∥≤ε for nx∈NX(x),ny∈NY(y). M=1+Z(Gy+1)/δ, B=1+μ+Lf+MLJ+J, Δ=GxDX+GyDY+MC, S=1+m+M. In (2), Ma=mC+Z(1+Gy+DY+JC)/δ, A=max{1,Ma,Ma(Ma+C)}, ℓε=1+μ+Lf+LJC+(LJC+J2)A/ε, and H=1+GxDX+GyDY+Gx2+Gy2+(1+μ)DY2+C2. Bounds suppress universal factors; the fixed-data order in (3) suppresses dependence on its other parameters. Uniform inner Slater means ci(x,y^x)≤−δd<0 uniformly in x,i.

Lu, Zhaosong, and Sanyou Mei. 2026. A First-Order Method for Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Constrained Minimax Optimization. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2512.22909.
Zhang, Huiling, Minhao Zhang, Zi Xu, and Yu-Hong Dai. 2026. ALDER: A Single-Loop Augmented-Lagrangian Damped Extragradient Method for Nonconvex–Concave Minimax Problems with Nonlinear Coupled Constraints. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2611.00691.
source:
import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Adjoint
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.ProdL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Basic

open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.CoupledStronglyConcaveMinimax

structure Params where
  nx : ℕ
  ny : ℕ
  constraints : ℕ
  X : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin nx))
  Y : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin ny))
  x0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin nx)
  y0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin ny)
  Lf : ℝ
  LJ : ℝ
  J : ℝ
  Gx : ℝ
  Gy : ℝ
  C : ℝ
  DX : ℝ
  DY : ℝ
  μ : ℝ
  δ : ℝ
  Z : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev XSpace (p : Params) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.nx)
abbrev YSpace (p : Params) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.ny)
abbrev Weights (p : Params) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.constraints)
abbrev Joint (p : Params) := WithLp 2 (XSpace p × YSpace p)

def domain (p : Params) : Set (Joint p) := {z | z.fst ∈ p.X ∧ z.snd ∈ p.Y}

def Normal {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    (S : Set E) (x n : E) : Prop := ∀ u ∈ S, ⟪n, u - x⟫ ≤ 0

structure Valid (p : Params) : Prop where
  compactX : IsCompact p.X
  compactY : IsCompact p.Y
  convexX : Convex ℝ p.X
  convexY : Convex ℝ p.Y
  startX : p.x0 ∈ p.X
  startY : p.y0 ∈ p.Y
  diameterX : ∀ x ∈ p.X, ∀ x' ∈ p.X, ‖x - x'‖ ≤ p.DX
  diameterY : ∀ y ∈ p.Y, ∀ y' ∈ p.Y, ‖y - y'‖ ≤ p.DY
  Lf_nonneg : 0 ≤ p.Lf
  LJ_nonneg : 0 ≤ p.LJ
  J_nonneg : 0 ≤ p.J
  Gx_nonneg : 0 ≤ p.Gx
  Gy_nonneg : 0 ≤ p.Gy
  C_nonneg : 0 ≤ p.C
  DX_nonneg : 0 ≤ p.DX
  DY_nonneg : 0 ≤ p.DY
  μ_pos : 0 < p.μ
  δ_pos : 0 < p.δ
  Z_pos : 0 < p.Z
  ε_pos : 0 < p.ε

structure Instance (p : Params) where
  f : Joint p → ℝ
  c : Joint p → Weights p
  g : Joint p → Joint p
  jac : Joint p → (Joint p →L[ℝ] Weights p)

structure Assumptions (p : Params) (I : Instance p) : Prop where
  gradient : ∀ z ∈ domain p, HasGradientAt I.f (I.g z) z
  derivative : ∀ z ∈ domain p, HasFDerivAt I.c (I.jac z) z
  gradient_lipschitz : ∀ z ∈ domain p, ∀ w ∈ domain p,
    ‖I.g z - I.g w‖ ≤ p.Lf * ‖z - w‖
  jacobian_lipschitz : ∀ z ∈ domain p, ∀ w ∈ domain p,
    ‖I.jac z - I.jac w‖ ≤ p.LJ * ‖z - w‖
  jacobian_bound : ∀ z ∈ domain p, ‖I.jac z‖ ≤ p.J
  gradientX_bound : ∀ z ∈ domain p, ‖(I.g z).fst‖ ≤ p.Gx
  gradientY_bound : ∀ z ∈ domain p, ‖(I.g z).snd‖ ≤ p.Gy
  constraint_bound : ∀ z ∈ domain p, ‖I.c z‖ ≤ p.C
  convex_constraints : ∀ x ∈ p.X, ∀ i,
    ConvexOn ℝ p.Y (fun y => I.c (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y)) i)
  strongly_concave : ∀ x ∈ p.X, ∀ y ∈ p.Y, ∀ y' ∈ p.Y,
    I.f (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y')) ≤ I.f (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y)) +
      ⟪(I.g (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y))).snd, y' - y⟫ - p.μ / 2 * ‖y' - y‖ ^ 2
  qualification : ∀ z ∈ domain p, ∃ d : YSpace p, ‖d‖ ≤ p.Z ∧
    (∀ n, Normal p.Y z.snd n → ⟪n, d⟫ ≤ 0) ∧
    ∀ i, 0 < I.c z i → (I.jac z (WithLp.toLp 2 (0, d))) i ≤ -p.δ

structure Reply (p : Params) where
  value : ℝ
  gradient : Joint p
  constraints : Weights p
  jacobian : Joint p →L[ℝ] Weights p

structure Output (p : Params) where
  x : XSpace p
  y : YSpace p
  multiplier : Weights p

noncomputable def exactReply (p : Params) (I : Instance p) (z : Joint p) : Reply p :=
  ⟨I.f z, I.g z, I.c z, I.jac z⟩

noncomputable def KKT (p : Params) (I : Instance p) (o : Output p) : Prop :=
  let z := WithLp.toLp 2 (o.x, o.y)
  let g := I.g z - (I.jac z).adjoint o.multiplier
  o.x ∈ p.X ∧ o.y ∈ p.Y ∧ (∀ i, 0 ≤ o.multiplier i) ∧
    ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => max (I.c z i) 0)‖ ≤ p.ε ∧
    (∑ i, |o.multiplier i * I.c z i|) ≤ p.ε ∧
    ∃ nx ny, Normal p.X o.x nx ∧ Normal p.Y o.y ny ∧
      ‖g.fst + nx‖ ≤ p.ε ∧ ‖g.snd - ny‖ ≤ p.ε

abbrev spec : OracleTemplate.Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance := Instance
  Query := Joint
  Reply := Reply
  Output := Output
  publicInput := id
  valid := Valid
  admissible p I oracle := Assumptions p I ∧
    ∀ history seed z, z ∈ domain p → oracle.answer history (0, z) seed = exactReply p I z
  successful p I output law := ∀ᵐ ω ∂(law : MeasureTheory.Measure _), KKT p I (output ω)

end LongTails.Setups.CoupledStronglyConcaveMinimax
